label: Tsigai

names.text: The alternative names are as given in the item's known list, from the Wikipedia article on the breed; not separately confirmed on a second page.

about.text: The Tsigai is a Romanian dairy sheep breed, also kept in Hungary, where it is found in Körös-Maros National Park and on private farms. Its milk supports cheesemaking, and the old type was milked for 5 to 6 months and also used for meat and wool.

sources.text: Hungarian keeping, milking period, cheesemaking and the old type's meat and wool use are all from the Wikipedia article. The article is flagged as needing more citations.

origin.place: Southern Moldavia and Dobrogea in Romania, later spreading to Transylvania through transhumant Mocan shepherds

sources.text: Place and the spread to Transylvania from the Wikipedia article. The article says the breed is thought to descend from sheep domesticated around the eastern Black Sea. No year of formation is given.
The old Tsigai is milk, meat and wool (wool used in the textile industry); the domestic Tsigai is milk, used in cheesemaking. Dairy is listed first because the brief names it as a dairy breed.

facts.v: The old, native Tsigai can yield 40 to 60 litres of milk over a 5 to 6 month milking period.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article's description of the old type; no year is given.

facts.v: The domestic Tsigai yields 110 to 120 litres in the milking period, which the article does not state in length.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article's description of the domestic type; no year and no milking-period length given.

facts.v: The domestic Tsigai has been recorded as a separate breed since 1999 and has been a protected breed since 2008.

sources.text: From the Wikipedia article; it names no official registry for these dates, so treat them as the article's claim.

gaps: Milk composition (fat, protein, lactose, solids) not found. No DAD-IS entry was found by search or fetch, so there is no population figure with a year and no FAO risk status. The Hungarian count (about 10,000 females and 50 males) has no year. No year of formation found. The Wikipedia article gives litres, not kilograms, and its figures are undated; they could not be checked against a primary source.
